\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Bernoulli Cost}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.LMN.BernoulliCost
\section{Overview}
This module compares the fixed-size restriction model $R_k$ (uniform over restrictions
with exactly $k$ free variables) with the Bernoulli restriction model $R_p$, and shows
that switching from $R_k$ to $R_p$ costs nothing asymptotically: if the bad event has
probability at most $(5kw/n)^s$ under every $R_k$, then under $R_p$ it has probability at
most $(10pw)^s$ plus an exponentially small tail $e^{-np/3}$ that vanishes as $n \to \infty$.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Restrictions with a fixed number of free variables]
\lean{BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrs}
\statementsource{switching-lemma}{pdf-b5e074215b9e-p001-b007}
\label{BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrs}
\leanok
\uses{SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction.freeVars}
For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, this is the finite set of restrictions on $n$ variables
whose set of free variables has cardinality exactly $k$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Fixed-size restriction probability $R_k$]
\lean{BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrProb}
\statementsource{switching-lemma}{pdf-b5e074215b9e-p001-b007}
\label{BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrProb}
\leanok
\uses{BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrs, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction}
The probability of an event under the fixed-size restriction model $R_k$, which is uniform
over restrictions with exactly $k$ free variables. It is defined as the fraction of
restrictions with exactly $k$ free variables that satisfy the event.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Binomial probability mass function]
\lean{BernoulliCost.binomialPMF}
\label{BernoulliCost.binomialPMF}
\leanok
The binomial probability mass function, $\Pr[\mathrm{Bin}(n,p) = k] = \binom{n}{k}\, p^k\, (1-p)^{n-k}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegativity of the fixed-size restriction probability]
\lean{BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrProb_nonneg}
\label{BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrProb_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction}
\difficulty{1}
Fix natural numbers $n$ and $k$, and let $E$ be any event on restrictions of $n$
variables. Then the probability of $E$ under the fixed-size restriction model $R_k$ —
the uniform distribution over restrictions with exactly $k$ free variables — is
nonnegative:
\[
0 \le R_k(E).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Fixed-size restriction probability is at most one]
\lean{BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrProb_le_one}
\label{BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrProb_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrProb, BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrs, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction}
\difficulty{3}
Let $E$ be any event, that is, a property of restrictions on $n$ variables, and let $k$
be a natural number. Under the fixed-size restriction model $R_k$ — the uniform
distribution over those restrictions on $n$ variables whose set of free variables has
cardinality exactly $k$ — the probability of $E$ satisfies $R_k(E) \le 1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegativity of the binomial mass function]
\lean{BernoulliCost.binomialPMF_nonneg}
\label{BernoulliCost.binomialPMF_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{BernoulliCost.binomialPMF}
\difficulty{2}
Fix a natural number $n$ and a real number $p$ with $0 \le p \le 1$. Then for every
natural number $k$, the binomial probability mass value $\binom{n}{k}\, p^k\,
(1-p)^{n-k}$ is nonnegative.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Binomial probability mass function sums to one]
\lean{BernoulliCost.binomialPMF_sum_one}
\label{BernoulliCost.binomialPMF_sum_one}
\leanok
\uses{BernoulliCost.binomialPMF}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $p$ be a real number with $0 \le p \le 1$. Then the
binomial probabilities $\binom{n}{k}\, p^k\, (1-p)^{n-k}$ sum to one over all outcomes,
\[\sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k}\, p^k\, (1-p)^{n-k} = 1.\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Decomposition of Bernoulli restriction probability by free-variable count]
\lean{BernoulliCost.bernoulli_decompose}
\label{BernoulliCost.bernoulli_decompose}
\leanok
\uses{BernoulliCost.binomialPMF, BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrProb, BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrs, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction.freeVars, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrWeight}
\difficulty{6}
Fix $n$ and a real parameter $p$ with $0 \le p \le 1$, and let $\mathrm{event}$ be any
(decidable) property of restrictions on $n$ variables. Then the probability that
$\mathrm{event}$ holds under a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction equals its average over
the fixed-size restriction models, weighted by the binomial distribution on the number
of free variables:
\[
\Pr_{p}[\mathrm{event}] \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k}\, p^{k}\, (1-p)^{\,n-k}\;
R_k(\mathrm{event}),
\]
where $R_k(\mathrm{event})$ is the fraction of restrictions with exactly $k$ free
variables that satisfy $\mathrm{event}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Chernoff upper-tail bound for the binomial distribution]
\lean{BernoulliCost.chernoff_binomial_upper_tail}
\label{BernoulliCost.chernoff_binomial_upper_tail}
\leanok
\uses{BernoulliCost.binomialPMF}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $p$ be a real number with $0 < p \le 1$. Summing the
binomial probability mass function $\binom{n}{k}\,p^k\,(1-p)^{n-k}$ over those integers
$k \in \{0, 1, \dots, n\}$ satisfying $k > 2np$ yields at most $e^{-np/3}$; that is, the
probability that $\mathrm{Bin}(n,p)$ exceeds twice its mean is bounded by $e^{-np/3}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Bernoulli restriction cost bound]
\lean{BernoulliCost.bernoulli_restriction_cost}
\label{BernoulliCost.bernoulli_restriction_cost}
\leanok
\uses{BernoulliCost.bernoulli_decompose, BernoulliCost.binomialPMF, BernoulliCost.binomialPMF_nonneg, BernoulliCost.binomialPMF_sum_one, BernoulliCost.chernoff_binomial_upper_tail, BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrProb, BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrProb_le_one, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n \ge 1$, let $p \in \bbr$ satisfy $0 < p \le 1$, and let $w, s$ be positive
integers. Let $\mathrm{event}$ be a decidable predicate on restrictions of $n$
variables, and suppose that for every $k \le n$ its probability under the fixed-size
restriction model $R_k$ satisfies
\[
  \Pr_{R_k}[\mathrm{event}] \le \left(\frac{5kw}{n}\right)^{s}.
\]
Then the probability of $\mathrm{event}$ under a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction
satisfies
\[
  \Pr_{R_p}[\mathrm{event}] \le (10\,p\,w)^{s} + \exp\!\left(-\frac{n\,p}{3}\right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Eventual smallness of an exponential tail]
\lean{BernoulliCost.exp_neg_eventually_small}
\label{BernoulliCost.exp_neg_eventually_small}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every real $p > 0$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists a natural number $N$
such that for all natural numbers $m \ge N$ one has
\[
\exp\!\left(-\tfrac{mp}{3}\right) < \varepsilon.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Bernoulli restriction cost, asymptotic version]
\lean{BernoulliCost.bernoulli_restriction_asymptotic}
\label{BernoulliCost.bernoulli_restriction_asymptotic}
\leanok
\uses{BernoulliCost.bernoulli_restriction_cost, BernoulliCost.exp_neg_eventually_small, BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb}
\difficulty{3}
Fix a parameter $p$ with $0 < p \le 1$, positive integers $w, s > 0$, and a tolerance
$\varepsilon > 0$. Then there exists $N \in \bbn$ such that for every $n \ge N$ with $n
> 0$ and every decidable event on restrictions of $n$ variables, the following holds: if
the fixed-size restriction probability satisfies
\[
R_k[\mathrm{event}] \le \left(\frac{5\,k\,w}{n}\right)^{s} \qquad \text{for every } k
\le n,
\]
then the probability of the event under a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction satisfies
\[
  \Pr_{p}[\mathrm{event}] \le (10\,p\,w)^{s} + \varepsilon.
\]
\end{theorem}
